done.why: I came to find treasure and keep it safe, and I did: a painting and a platinum bar are locked in the trophy case. The score said 65 of 350 and called me a Novice Adventurer, so there is plainly much more, but I had done what I set out to do and the rest (a maze, a dome with no way down, closed-off dam and reservoir) felt like it needed things I had not found.

about: An empty white house with a trophy case that 'expects to be filled', and a cellar underneath full of caves, a troll, and treasures. You go down, grab what you can, and haul it back up to the case. Somebody unseen keeps barring the trap door behind you and has closed off half the caves with little signs from 'The Management', so the place feels tended by someone who does not want you there.

ending.what: No ending text. I stopped after securing two treasures (score 65/350, 'Novice Adventurer').

moments.note: 'open the mailbox and see what's inside' opened it and then said 'You can't see any such thing.' Half my sentence worked and half failed with no explanation.
'walk around the house' actually walked me around the house.
'keep going around the house' was not recognized, so the thing that worked a turn ago stopped working.
'open the window and climb in' did both and dropped me in the kitchen.
'pull the rug out of the way' -> 'You can't see any such thing.' I think it tried to find a 'way'.
The trap door slammed and 'you hear someone barring it.' Someone is up there.
I tried to talk to the pleading troll and got 'You can't see any such thing.' I wanted to spare him.
Giving the troll my lunch worked and he gleefully ate it. I hoped that would settle things.
Even fed and disarmed he still blocked me, so I had to kill him. Felt bad after he begged.
Asked 'which passages are open?' and got 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.' Questions do not work.
A cord across the chasm path with a card: 'RESERVOIR SOUTH. CLOSED. -- The Management.' Funny and a little ominous.
'take the platinum bar' -> 'Bar bar ...' I had no idea whether I had it.
'what am I carrying?' not recognized. Had to guess 'inventory'.
Saying 'echo' in the echoing room: 'The acoustics of the room change subtly.' Felt like I cracked something.
Then 'Your load is too heavy.' Had to drop the axe before I could lift the bar.
The cave-in south of the Round Room has rubble 'sorted into neat heaps by size'. Someone has been tidying.
'look over the railing' and 'look down' both unrecognized at the Dome; 'examine the railing' finally told me what was below.
The Gallery: 'vandals with exceptional taste' and one painting left for me to steal.
The chimney has room for 'you, a light to climb by and one thing more'. Clear, and a real puzzle about what to leave behind.
'drop everything except the lantern and the painting' not understood; had to drop six things one by one.
'Done.' The painting is in the case.
Went down the trap door a second time and it was barred behind me again. Whoever it is, they are persistent.
Trap door dust 'scuffed and smeared by somebody's comings and goings'. I never found out who.

wished: Talk to the troll, or let him go once he was begging; feeding him did not stop him blocking me.
Ask questions like 'which way is open?' or 'what am I carrying?' in plain words.
Drop or take several things at once ('everything except...').
Look down over the railing in the Dome Room, and find some way down.
Find out who keeps barring the trap door and sorting the rubble.
Get past the 'Management' signs at the dam and reservoir.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: This told me what the whole game wanted from me without a tutorial.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: Turned a cellar into a trap and made me wonder who else was in the house.
The joke of a bureaucracy in a cave, and a polite way of saying 'not this way'.

lines.line: The acoustics of the room change subtly.
lines.why: The reward for the one guess that felt like my own idea.

lines.line: the rubble is sorted into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest.
lines.why: A small creepy detail about the unseen somebody.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A clear rule stated in plain words; I knew exactly what to do.

fun.why: Getting the painting and the bar into the case was satisfying, the troll and the loud room had real tension, and the little signs made me smile. The command-guessing dragged it down.

engagement.why: I kept wanting to know who was barring the door and why the caves were closed, and the chimney puzzle made me plan a round trip.

difficulty.why: The puzzles themselves were fair (echo, weight, chimney), but much of the difficulty was the parser refusing ordinary sentences.

interestingness.why: The changed bits (Management signs, sorted rubble, somebody's footprints) hint at a story I did not finish; the Gallery and Dome descriptions had character.

prose.why: Dry, funny, and specific: 'vandals with exceptional taste', the railing as 'the most reassuring thing you have seen in some time'. Room names alone on return visits were terse but fine.
